parts.note_add: Aftermarket motor-only replacement: Four Seasons 35483 (interchanges Mazda 8871-76-453 / 8871-76-453A, Cardone reman 44-1064, UAC BM3733, Siemens PM3733); it comes without the fan wheel, so the wheel is moved over from the old motor. Fed from the 20 A BLOWER fuse on the LO wire; speed is set by the resistor pack in the ground side.
The 1985 workshop manual (Section 15, p15-79) has an exploded view of the heater unit, blower unit and ducts; the 1985 dash differs, so use it for layout only.
The Mazda core 8871-76-402 is no longer available (Atkins Rotary). The Brassworks makes a copper replacement to order for 1979-85 LHD cars, about 12 to 14 weeks.
Genuine Mazda valve 8871-76-409 fits every 1979-85 12A and 13B car; Atkins Rotary lists it again (Mazda re-released it), stock varies. Mazdatrix lists it as NLA.
Engine-to-firewall heater hose, 1979-82 12A and 1984-85 13B; still sold new as genuine Mazda (Atkins Rotary, Mazdatrix).
Heater (at the firewall) to heater pipe hose, all 1979-85; still sold new as genuine Mazda.

Heater pipe to radiator hose, 1979-82 only; discontinued by Mazda (Atkins, Mazdatrix). Atkins says it takes hose clamp 9928-22-600. The 1983-85 hose FA42-61-213A is still sold but belongs to the '83 pipe.
Steel pipe that joins heater hose no. 2 to hose no. 3 (pipe to radiator); the 1979-82 pipe F001-61-220B is not the same as the '83 FA42-61-220C.

Three controls: a mode lever (REC/MAX, VENT, BI-LEVEL, HEAT, DEF), a temperature lever (COLD to HOT) and a rotary fan knob (OFF, L, M, HI) with the A/C push switch. This layout is shown on the 1980 panel (1980 workshop manual Fig. 15-33); check it against this car's panel.
Factory ref E-06, fed on RL from the panel dimmer and grounded on B; the 1.4 W rating is already recorded. Trade number not found: check it on the bulb.

Rotary 4-position switch (OFF, LO, MI, HI) that switches the blower's ground through the resistor taps. It also contains the A/C push switch and a 1.4 W A/C indicator lamp, so the A/C works only when the fan is on.

Adjusting (1985 manual, other panel): set the mode to VENT, pull the heater-unit mode lever fully rearward and clamp the wire. For temperature, set COLD MAX, push the heater-unit selector lever down (COLD) and clamp, then check it travels fully from COLD to HOT.
Under the passenger side of the dash. It holds the motor, fan, resistor pack and the fresh/recirculation door.
Aftermarket motors (Four Seasons 35483) come without a wheel, so this wheel is moved over to the new motor.

Mazda 8871-76-457 is no longer available (Atkins Rotary). A wire-wound pack in the blower unit under the passenger dash. On A/C cars the first stage is shorted, so HI runs the motor with no resistance. Owners report that 40-year-old packs go open-circuit; rx7club suggests the 1986 Mazda 626 or 323 pack as a donor (unverified).
Carries the blower unit's 4-pin connector G-14 (LO, LR, LY, LW), which links the dash harness to the motor and the resistor taps.

specs.note: OFF, LO, MI and HI through the resistor pack; the motor feed is IG through the 20 A BLOWER fuse on LO.
Motor only, without wheel; interchanges Mazda 887176453 / 887176453A. Two lead wires, flanged, vented, rotation listed as CW/CCW.

In series from the motor's ground side: stage 1 to the HI tap (LY), stage 2 to the MI tap (LR), stage 3 to the LO tap (LW). S-001 marks stage 1 'short with air-con': on an A/C car (this car) HI gets no resistance. Ohm values are not given in any source found; measure them.

specs.note: 1985 workshop manual (1984-85 panel). Then run the blower at HI with temperature at COLD and check that no air leaks from the floor outlets.

specs.value: Knob at COLD MAX, heater-unit selector lever pushed down (COLD), then clamp; check full travel COLD to HOT
